title: Development of the model of cold rolling process in dynamic conditions
authors: Aleksandr V. Kozhevnikov; Irina A. Kozhevnikova; Nataliya L. Bolobanova
version: JCTM 53(2), 2018, published citation pp.366–372; reviewed author-uploaded manuscript, uploaded 2018-10-11, internal pp.11–17 with provisional publication pagination. Publisher PDF search-indexed but direct retrieval failed. Manuscript/version-of-record equivalence not verified.
pages_equations_tables: Author manuscript pp.11–17, model/results/conclusions; Eqs.1–11, Table1 and figure captions. Equation OCR incomplete; plotted figures not visually audited.
findings: Couples elastoplastic bite, neighbouring stands and drive torque feedback. Eqs.9–11 introduce inertia, two-mass transmission/backlash and DC electrical states. Eq.4 separates rolling, bearing, backup-roll and tension torque.
Table1 supplies a Severstal five-stand steel schedule; Fig.4 describes measured-versus-modelled stand-2 force. Tension entries are forces in kN. Ramp/weld and steady regimes are distinguished.
weaknesses_conflicts: Manuscript contains an unfinished sentence and provisional pages. Eq.5 divides power by omega, called peripheral velocity in prose but angular velocity in Fig.1: dimensional reconciliation required. Retranscribe Eq.8 signs/factor and Eq.10 backlash branches from verified original.

No public raw oscillograms, quantified validation uncertainty or universal model-enable thresholds established. No aluminium validation. Distinct publication from R169; shared authors/evidence do not make independent replications.
domain: Steel tandem cold strip; no established aluminium/foil/pack domain
evidence_level: Primary modelling and industrial comparison; incomplete author-manuscript verification
relevance: Basis for a future coupled transient model and unit audit; cannot supply plant limits or executable equations without reconciliation.
provenance: New targeted operational search; not a recovered historical bibliography item.

title: Simulation of Cold-Rolling Process in Dynamic Conditions
authors: A. V. Kozhevnikov; I. A. Kozhevnikova; N. L. Bolobanova
version: Metallurgist 61(7–8), 519–522, published 2017-11-20; published English translation of Metallurg No.7 pp.15–18 July2017, author-uploaded 2018-06-18. Original and translation belong to one work identity; separate from JCTM R167.
pages_equations_tables: pp.519–522 body, Tables1–2, Figs.1–4 captions; graph pixels not independently read.
findings: Coupled deformation/interstand, hydraulic hold-down and electromechanical models; roll-speed/torque feedback and force/gap coupling distinguish this from independent snapshots.
08ps steel industrial oscillography: reported shaft-speed mean error3.5%, maximum6.6%; force error within6% in85.3% of cases. Table2 tensions are MPa, unlike force variables in Fig.1.
weaknesses_conflicts: Model details delegated to references; raw time series, sample counts, uncertainty and controller activation logic not established. Random yield/thickness spreads are assumed optimisation inputs. Reported8% energy improvement is a simulated schedule comparison, not independently demonstrated plant savings.
Same research group/mill as R167; correlated evidence. Neither validates aluminium, thermal feedback, rate constitutive response, pack rolling or live-control safety.
evidence_level: Primary simulation with reported industrial time-series comparison; incomplete reproducibility
relevance: Specify measurable dynamic states and benchmark outputs; keep steady and transient error measures separate.
provenance: New targeted operational search; selected for accessible primary dynamic evidence.

title: Synergistic optimization of shape-force and dynamic coupling effect in bending roll systems during accelerated rolling
authors: Zhu-wen Yan; Ying-xin Tang; Shuai-zhen Pan; Wen-jun Cao; Jia-wei Wu
version: Scientific Reports 15, article38073, published 2025-10-30; publisher HTML. Supplement spreadsheet linked but not read (tool unsupported binary, shell retrieval403).
pages_equations_tables: Model creation/grid/preliminary results; dynamic compensation Eq.6; industrial verification; Table4 independently opened; Tables6–7 and supplement links located. Selected body read, figures not visually audited.
findings: Sequential ABAQUS stand-state transfer and speed-segment bending/tension compensation. Reported industrial trial concerns steel. This does not establish simultaneous interstand drive/tension dynamics or validated thermal/rate feedback.
weaknesses_conflicts: Reduction adjusted for model comparison: calibration is not independent validation. Main prose2.102/2.0mm implies5.1%, not stated2.53%; Table4 instead2.066/2.015mm consistently gives2.53%. Preserve both, quarantine prose. Table4 flatness error25%.

Second-order hexahedral mesh and explicit-analysis statements require exact element/solver clarification. Trial uncertainty, sample count and public raw traces not established. No transferable enable thresholds; speed segmentation is not a universal controller recipe.
domain: Steel, six-high stands/five-stand cold tandem line; aluminium transfer unvalidated
evidence_level: Primary FE/industrial report, methodological and numerical ambiguities
relevance: Motivates offline shape-versus-speed studies; not an accepted accuracy benchmark or source of aluminium limits.
provenance: New targeted operational search; DOI identity checked against current ledger.
